categories.regulatorik: EU AI Act, GDPR, UWG and compliance

entries.definition: A way of working where AI tools are a fixed part of a defined process. Judgement, review and accountability stay with people.
Anthropic's family of AI models.
Anthropic's web interface for Claude, with Projects, Artifacts, connectors and memory depending on the plan.
An agentic coding tool with controlled access to files and development tools. It can use permitted Skills, plugins, MCP servers and subagents.
A Claude.ai workspace that groups instructions, files and conversations for one area of work.
A reusable instruction package for a recurring task, with guidance, permitted tools and resources.
An installable package of Skills, MCP servers, hooks or subagents. Check its contents and permissions before you use it.
An authorised link between an AI interface and an external source.
Model Context Protocol, an open protocol that connects AI applications to external tools and resources through defined interfaces.
A local or remote service that exposes tools or resources over MCP. Its security depends on code, permissions and operation.
A separate Claude.ai view for longer outputs such as documents, code or graphics.
A frontend-design workflow from the course that settles layout and interaction before implementation.
Product features that keep selected context across conversations.
A Markdown file with project context, conventions and limits that Claude Code can load from the project hierarchy. Keep it current and free of secrets.
A Claude model name used in the course.
A Claude model name used in the course.
A course reference to a smaller Claude model. Once tested, it can suit bounded, high-volume tasks.
Projects, Areas, Resources and Archives: Tiago Forte's method for sorting knowledge into four parts.
Map of Content: an index note that links a project's material and can record its status.
A maintained external knowledge system; in this course, an Obsidian vault whose notes tools can search and review.
Reviewing new notes at the end of a session and moving them out of the Obsidian inbox.
A dated work note used as a scratchpad and link index.
An Obsidian community plugin for creating and updating notes from templates.
An Obsidian community plugin for querying metadata and content across a vault.
An Obsidian plugin that can use embeddings to show related notes.
An Obsidian plugin for model-assisted chat and retrieval over vault content.
Obsidian's browser extension that saves web content to a vault, optionally with templates or AI interpretation.
An MCP integration that gives Claude Code access to an Obsidian vault. Review its code, permissions and network access before use.
Numerical representations for comparing the semantic similarity of items such as text passages.
A source-available workflow-automation platform with a node-based visual editor and self-hosting options.
The event or schedule that starts a workflow, such as a webhook, schedule, polling or application event.
A workflow step that prepares or performs an operation such as an API request, review draft or database write. In production it needs permissions, approval and failure handling.
A sequence of triggers, decisions and actions. The course simulates them; in production they need versioning, monitoring, access control and recovery.
An HTTP endpoint for events from another system. Depending on use it needs authentication or signature checks, input validation and replay protection.
Software on infrastructure the organisation chooses itself. It can increase control but on its own proves neither security nor GDPR compliance.
A German cloud host with data centres in Germany and other regions. Compliance depends on location, contract and configuration.
A desktop app that downloads and runs language models locally.
A tool that downloads models and runs them locally through the command line and a local API.
Meta's family of language models. Check each model's licence, size, hardware needs and intended use before you run it.
Running a model on the organisation's own hardware instead of a hosted API. It saves some data transfers but still needs access control, logging and maintenance.
A meeting transcription and notes service. Check languages, hosting regions, subprocessors and retention for your plan.
A search product that answers with linked sources. Check the original sources before you rely on an answer.
A course model in which a person sets the task and controls and Claude runs bounded steps. The person reviews and owns the result.
An older course term for structured use: a clear brief, relevant context, limited permissions, a fixed review step. The model replaces neither a person nor their accountability.
One of the three course patterns: the model writes the first draft, a person edits and approves the next version.
Course pattern: the model finds structure and returns set fields in a fixed format for review.
Course pattern: the model sorts information against clear questions and names sources that are then checked directly.
A briefing structure of Role, Context, Task, Format and Constraints, usable as a checklist.
Asking a model for step-by-step reasoning. For a review, ask for brief assumptions, evidence and a checkable rationale, not internal reasoning.
A few examples before the actual input so the model follows their format or classification rule.
Model output constrained to a fixed schema such as JSON, CSV or Markdown so it can be validated and processed further.

An attack in which untrusted input tries to override instructions or trigger unsafe tool use. Separate trust zones, minimal permissions, checked inputs and outputs, and approval for consequential actions help.
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, which establishes rules for AI systems in the European Union through a phased application schedule.
Annex III to the EU AI Act lists use cases that may be classified as high-risk when the regulation's conditions and exceptions are met.
An AI system classified as high-risk under the EU AI Act, including qualifying systems covered by Annex I or Annex III. Applicable duties depend on the system, role and use case.

Under the EU AI Act, a person or organisation that develops an AI system or general-purpose AI model, or has one developed, and places it on the market or puts it into service under its own name or trademark.
Under the EU AI Act, a person or organisation using an AI system under its authority, except for personal non-professional use. In a company, the organisation is generally the deployer.
A person or organisation located in the EU that places an AI system bearing the name or trademark of a non-EU entity on the EU market.
Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment. Article 27 of the EU AI Act requires one for specified deployers and qualifying high-risk uses, not for every AI deployment.

Article 4 of the EU AI Act requires providers and deployers to take measures supporting the development of AI literacy among their staff and others acting on their behalf. Knowledge, experience, education and training, use context and affected people or groups must be considered; no specific individual level has to be guaranteed. This course can be one measure among several.
Germany's Act Against Unfair Competition. Section 5 covers misleading commercial practices, including unsupported quantitative claims.
The German abbreviation for the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which governs processing of personal data in the EU and EEA.
A data processing agreement under GDPR Article 28 between a controller and a processor when the processor handles personal data on the controller's behalf.
GDPR Article 22 concerns certain decisions based solely on automated processing that produce legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its conditions and exceptions.
German administrative principles for keeping and retaining accounting records in electronic form. Applicable retention periods depend on the record type and current law.
A German accreditation and approval regulation for employment-support services. This open course explains the term but makes no funding claim.
Germany's Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control. This open learning platform does not claim a BAFA funding or booking arrangement.
The course's final project: document and test one small workflow, then assess it against a rubric.
The free predecessor course. It supports Article 4 AI literacy, data classification and prompting basics, but does not replace a complete internal Article 4 process.
Supporting material on vault structures, Skill patterns, prompt examples, n8n exercises, MCP guidance and CLAUDE.md starters.
